fieldNotes.siteResolution: Supplied coords (43.5950,-70.6450) landed ~9.5km too far south, inside the Killick Pond Estates wooded residential subdivision (verified: forest + scattered houses at z14-z17, no industrial building). Geocoding 400 Killick Pond Rd, Hollis ME 04042 via the Maps API returned 43.67630,-70.64120, which resolves on satellite to a single ~700k-sqft white-roofed industrial bottling plant with a large multi-hundred-trailer drop yard, a solar farm to the SW, and a Killick Pond Rd frontage. Web-confirmed as the Nestle Waters / Poland Spring (now Primo Brands / BlueTriton) Hollis Factory, opened 2000, the largest water bottling facility in the US (12 bottling lines), with an adjacent 13MW / 50-acre / 23,000-module solar array. Locked building center 43.67630,-70.64190.
fieldNotes.truckGate: FALSE. Street View on Killick Pond Rd at the property entrance (pano d4G11FtE34bCPsE3YZTMCw, Nov 2024) looking up the access drive shows a wide, fully open, paved entry with painted lane channelization but NO barrier arm, NO sliding/swing gate, and NO perimeter fence at the frontage - open grass between road and building. The painted island/hatching seen in z20 satellite at the entry throat is lane-divider channelization, not a controlled checkpoint. Marked false with high confidence from ground-level imagery.
fieldNotes.guardShack: FALSE. No booth-sized structure (1-3 vehicle footprint, multi-side windows) at the entrance in either satellite (z19-z20) or Street View. The only small structures near the SE corner are an office vestibule attached to the main building and light/sign poles. False, high confidence.
fieldNotes.remoteGs: FALSE - requires a truck gate to be present; there is no gate, so remote check-in does not apply.
fieldNotes.postGateStaging: TRUE. A very large internal paved apron and a long dedicated approach/staging lane (the wide asphalt strip running SW from the NW dock face) sit inside the property before the dock doors - ample internal queue space.
fieldNotes.drivewayLong: TRUE. The access drive from Killick Pond Rd plus the deep internal yard and the long SW approach lane easily hold a queue of 3+ trucks before reaching docks.
fieldNotes.entryExitTogether: TRUE. A single truck access point off Killick Pond Rd at the SE serves both in and out; the entry drive splits into channelized in/out lanes but at one property-line point.
fieldNotes.entryLanes: Estimated 2 - the entry throat shows painted channelization splitting into roughly two inbound lanes around a center island. Low confidence; banded from z20 markings.
fieldNotes.exitLanes: Estimated 1 outbound lane at the same throat. Low confidence.
fieldNotes.fastLaneOpportunity: TRUE. The entrance throat is very wide with painted islands and unused paved width, and the long SW approach lane provides abundant room to add an express/bypass lane - strong physical room for a fast lane.
fieldNotes.dockDoors: 50+. The NW (long) face of the building carries a continuous, full-length bank of dock doors with trailers backed in nose-to-tail (z18-z19 NE/SW face crops show 30-50+ trailers at dock along this face alone). Given the building length (~290m NW face) and ~12ft door spacing, total dock doors comfortably exceed 50; honest point estimate ~70. Banded 50+.
fieldNotes.dropArea: 50+. The NW drop yard holds many long parallel rows of unhitched trailers - z19 crops show 8-10 rows of ~10-15 trailers each, well over 100 parked trailers. Clearly the top band, 50+.
fieldNotes.dropYard: TRUE. A dedicated multi-acre trailer-storage lot on the NW side, distinct from the active dock apron, packed with parked trailers.
fieldNotes.shipRcvSeparate: FALSE (medium confidence). Docks are concentrated as one continuous bank on the NW building face; no clearly separate second dock cluster on a different face was identifiable, so ship/receive read as a single combined dock line. Cannot confirm internal function split from imagery.
fieldNotes.scale: FALSE. No truck scale / weigh pad or scale house identified in the truck path on z19-z20 imagery.
fieldNotes.trailersVisible: ~180 honest estimate: ~30-50 backed at the NW dock face + 100+ in the NW drop-yard rows + scattered units in the staging/approach lane. Approximate from overhead count across tiles.
fieldNotes.trailerParkingCapacity: ~220 - the drop-yard rows plus the deep approach/staging lane and apron could hold materially more than currently parked.
fieldNotes.siteAreaAcres: ~62 acres of cleared/paved operating footprint inside the treeline (building + drop yard + approach lane + parking + apron), derived from the perimeter polygon. Excludes the separate 50-acre solar array to the SW and the surrounding forest/spring land.
fieldNotes.buildingCount: 1 - one massive contiguous industrial building (bottling + warehouse under one roofline) with a minor attached office vestibule at the SE; counted as one.
fieldNotes.railServed: FALSE. No rail spur enters the property; access is road-only via Killick Pond Rd.
fieldNotes.connectivityIssue: FALSE. Although rural, the site is a major 24/7 industrial plant on a paved arterial with on-site solar/utility infrastructure and Street View LTE-era coverage; modern cellular coverage is expected. Marked false.
